subject: Renewal discussion: pricing options for PhoenixAI renewal and capacity uplift
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@phoenixai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion: pricing options for PhoenixAI renewal and capacity uplift

Hi Samira,

Thanks again for taking the time on Friday. Per our conversation I wanted to capture three practical pricing pathways so PhoenixAI has options while we align on capacity and term. High level summary below, attached usage export and a draft term sheet.

Current state: PhoenixAI is on a 12 month commit that averages ~2.2M tokens/month. You mentioned plans to expand to roughly 4M tokens/month over the next 9 months.

Options (illustrative):
- Option 1: 12 month renewal, modest uplift to committed tokens, 12% one-time renewal discount, standard SLAs
- Option 2: 24 month price-hold with stepped commit increases and a 10% credit up-front to offset migration/ingestion costs. Annual true-up to reconcile usage vs commit.
- Option 3: 24 month step-up commit with lower headline discount (6%) but additional burst buffer and a defined overage rate cap for first 6 months.

Asks from our side to provide a clean proposal: please confirm the expected target commit for 24 months (baseline and peak), and whether PhoenixAI needs a fixed price-hold across regions or only US.

Next step: happy to set a 30 minute pricing review this week. If you prefer, Marissa (cc) can prepare a formal sheet with numbers.

Attachments: Usage_Report_Q1.csv, PhoenixAI_Renewal_TermSheet_draft.pdf (see notes)

Best,
David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
M: (415) 555-0198

--
Requested internal routing: Marissa for pricing structure, Kimberly for finance approval once we have a path

From: Samira Khan <samira@phoenixai.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elliot Barnes <elliot@phoenixai.com>, contracts@phoenixai.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: pricing options for PhoenixAI renewal and capacity uplift

David,

Appreciate the clear options. High level feedback from our side:
- We are inclined towards a 24 month price-hold (Option 2) because predictability matters for our budget planning.
- We need clarity on how credits are applied across overages vs invoices, and whether the up-front credit reduces the committed spend or is processed as a one-time credit invoice.
- Region: primarily US for now; we could add EU later, but that should not be part of the initial price-hold.

Looping in Elliot from finance and our contracts address for the procurement path. Elliot, quick Q: is PhoenixAI comfortable with an annual true-up and invoice reconciliation cadence?

We will also want to see a worked example with your suggested commit profile (baseline -> peak) and the renewal math. If you can send the formal options and a short term-sheet we can fast-track internal approvals.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Director of Platform, PhoenixAI
samira@phoenixai.com

Subject: Internal: PhoenixAI renewal - need consolidated options and credit handling

Marissa, Kimberly,

Samira replied and is leaning to the 24 month price-hold (Option 2). They want specifics on credit mechanics and a worked example. Can you please prepare:

1) A formal term-sheet with three options (matching my bullets) including real $ examples based on the attached usage file.
2) A credit schedule: is the up-front credit applied against committed spend, or booked as a contra invoice? Provide cashflow implications.
3) A suggested audit clause and retention note — they asked about audit logs retention and who bears costs for longer retention windows.

Target: send to Samira and legal (cc'd on thread) by end of day Monday.

Marissa: quick thought on negotiation posture - offer a 10% up-front credit applied as a pre-paid credit against the first 6 months of overages, with an annual true-up and a conditional 2% renewal uplift if they breach the peak by >20%. This protects Redwood while giving PhoenixAI runway.

Kimberly: please confirm the accounting treatment and whether we can book the credit against invoice or need to treat it as a one-time service credit.

Thanks,
David

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@phoenixai.com>, Elliot Barnes <elliot@phoenixai.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, contracts@phoenixai.com
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: PhoenixAI - formalized options and term sheet (see attachments)

Hi Samira and Elliot,

Thanks for the prompt feedback. Attaching a concise term-sheet and a pricing options workbook that shows the math under three structured choices. Below is a short summary and the key commercial language we propose.

Option A - 12 month renewal
- Commit: 2.5M tokens/month
- One-time renewal discount: 12% applied as invoice credit over first 2 months
- No price-hold beyond 12 months

Option B - 24 month price-hold (recommended)
- Commit: baseline 2.5M tokens/month, step to 4.0M tokens/month at month 9
- Price-hold: 24 months for US region only
- Up-front credit: 10% of first year committed spend issued as invoice credit and applied to overages for first 6 months
- Annual true-up: reconcile actual usage vs committed annually; overages billed at capped overage rate of 0.60x list through month 6, then standard overage thereafter

Option C - 24 month step-up commit
- Lower headline discount (6%), but includes 25% burst buffer and a temporary overage cap for the first 90 days after step-up

Accounting note: Per finance guidance the up-front credit is recorded as a contra-revenue credit and will reduce recognized revenue in the quarter it is applied. If PhoenixAI prefers a non-contra credit, we can issue an independent credit memo to be applied against invoices. Happy to model either approach.

Attachments: PhoenixAI_Renewal_TermSheet_v2.pdf, Pricing_Options.xlsx

Please review and let us know if you'd like a short call to walk through the workbook. If the commercial language above works, we can incorporate a one-line change to the audit logs retention clause you flagged and circulate for signature.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Finance Director, Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira@phoenixai.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: pricing options for PhoenixAI renewal and capacity uplift

Team,

Thank you for the clear options and the fast turnaround. We reviewed Option B internally and would like to move forward with that path in principle. A couple of small asks before we sign:

1) Audit logs retention: can we extend the standard retention window by 90 days for logs related to customer troubleshooting at no additional charge?
2) Credit application: we prefer the up-front credit to be treated as a contra-revenue credit applied to invoice overages (your accounting proposal is fine).

If you can reflect the audit logs language and resend the term-sheet, we will do a 30 day internal review and aim to return countersignature within that window. Elliot - will you confirm approval from finance side?

Happy to schedule a quick 20 minute call Tuesday to finalize language.

Best,
Samira Khan
Director of Platform, PhoenixAI
